entries.EN: Well, it seems that the stash gave me a new direction to follow. I found a flash drive with what appears to be a diary used by Strelok's group. Despite the few entries, I could work out that the group had two other members: Ghost and Fang. The diary also mentioned a "mutual friend" but I don't know whether he was part of the group. He definitely helped them out, that's for sure. According to Ghost's entry, Fang died when they were ambushed. So, at last, I have something solid: the name of someone who definitely knows Strelok - Ghost. As for Strelok himself, he may be somewhere in the North of the Zone.

entries.EN: Mole said: "...follow the spiral staircase down into the room with the columns. Move across the room towards the exit and enter a large room with pipes in the ceiling. Go down to the second exit, enter the tunnel and turn left. There will be a right turn at the end. Go directly to the exit from the small room and turn right. Look for a hole in the left wall next to the words "Don't enter - you'll die". That's the entrance to Strelok's stash."

entries.EN:
Investigation report. 
 
For official use only. 
 
To SBU Colonel V.M. Kruchelnikov, head of project "TRUTH".
From Captain D.F. Maksimenko, Commander of "Search-2" group.
Memo. 
 
Our group consisting of 3 investigators and a squad of SBU Special Forces conducted a search operation at Agroprom, the former Research Institute for agriculture on radiation-affected soil, from 12.05.2012 to 25.05.2012. Most of the equipment and documentation was missing, however the few things we were able to find allow us to come to the following conclusion: over the period from 2005 to 2008, the Institute did not conduct any research in its official fields of study. All the results of its "work" sent to the Ministry of Agriculture were falsified. Simultaneously, the Institute's management, specifically Petr Danilovich Strizh, continued to receive state financing, equipment and consumables and transferred them to a laboratory designated X18 using forged consignment notes, which provided cover for the operation by indicating that the materials were being transferred to an auxiliary facility for experiments. X18 appears to be a code name adopted by the group of people implicated in this affair, since our database contains no mention of this laboratory. Judging by the analysis of the documents we found, this laboratory is located within an hour's drive from the Institute. It is likely to be a clandestine facility so I would request the involvement of our analytical department. The lab's field of research is not clear and available documents contain no helpful information in this regard but do make references to the infamous professor Chubko and also mention some "Group". It is my firm belief that we have come to the end of the line and the analytical department will now have plenty of work to do. 
 
Attached is an archived file containing consignment notes for consumable materials and equipment transferred to some auxiliary facility and an extract from correspondence between Strizh and Chubko. 
 
 Captain D.F. Maksimenko 26.05.2012 
 
To professor V.M. Chubko.
From P.D. Strizh, Head of Agroprom Research Institute, Doctor of Agricultural Sciences. 
 
 Dear Vadim Mikhailovich, As agreed, I am sending the next batch of consumable materials and equipment to our experimental facility to help you with your research, which is so essential for agriculture. I arranged financing for the experiments by describing them as pilot trials in fields studied by the Institute so there won't be any problems with the Ministry. How are the experiments progressing? I am still deeply impressed by the results you showed me last time. 
 
 Sincerely yours, P.D. Strizh, DAS. 
 
To P.D. Strizh,
 Please accept my gratitute, Petr Danilovich, we've received everything. My team is very impressed with the laser spectrometer - if not for you, it would take me eons to acquire this model through my channels. Of course the Ministry of Agriculture will be happy to receive OUR results... You really made an old man laugh with that one! The experiments are continuing exceptionally and the results you saw last time are dwarfed by our latest achievements. You should visit more often - I am always happy to see you and it's only an hour's drive to our "experimental facility" as you called it :) I almost forgot, I have news for you: next Monday I will be discussing your candidacy with the Group. I think they will support me.
 Sincerely yours, professor V.M. Chubko. 
 
To professor V.M. Chubko,
From P.D. Strizh, Head of Agroprom Research Institute, Doctor of Agricultural Sciences. 
 
 Dear Vadim Mikhailovich, thank you for your trust. I am touched and will do my best to prove you right. I think it is every scientist's greatest dream to have an opportunity to carry out such illustrious research free of limitations and restrictions. I will be absolutely delighted to be accepted into the Group.
Sincerely yours, P.D. Strizh. 
 
P.S. I managed to get two of the latest Japanese broadband oscilloscopes from the Ministry and will send them over at the earliest opportunity.

entries.EN: The chart details the patrols, sentries and guard towers. The HQ is on the third floor of the Institute. That's where the documents are kept. By day the area is saturated with patrols. There are fewer of them at night and the guards are relieved at 11pm. There are few people in the main building at this time. If you want to get into the base, you should make entry through the catacombs, the main gate is not an option.

entries.EN:
Received from Ghost: 
 
 Strelok, I have some shitty news. Fang died. They were waiting for us in the village by the warehouses, and I think they were waiting a long time. Three of them. Seems like your average neutrals. Fang sensed them somehow. You know full well he has a good sense. We ran two of them down - clearly bandits - but the third turned out smarter than his buddies. He was on over-watch with a Vintorez about a 100 meters away. Anyway, there's no more Fang. So next time we'll go to the center together, just the two of us. And here's another thing: those two had our descriptions. I can't figure out who would want us killed, although I can imagine quite a few heavy hitters may have something against us. The third one managed to get away - I think he may have been a merc. Had a big scar on his face. Hazel eyes. I'll try to find him. 
 So that's the deal. Keep an eye out and good luck. 
 Ghost 
 
 to Ghost 

 "Hey there buddy. 
 Leaving you some info, won't try to link up with you, noticed someone following me. 
 Dude, I went North... You know which place... Will try to make it through solo... Sorry but had no time to wait for you... Will explain later. 
 Trust me, that freak who killed Fang will be sorry he was ever born... I'll cut him apart... You find out who he is, and I'll be back soon - we'll settle our debt with him. 
 We're meeting at our mutual friend's place - you know who and where :) 
 Good luck. 
 Strelok” 
 
 To Strelok 
 
 “Hey. Came. You weren’t there. You shouldn’t have gone to the center alone. But no big deal. I know where and with whom to find you :) 
 Ghost”

entries.EN:
That's it, I'm done! I give up this stupid idea, let this expedition go to hell! Back and forth, then almost to the North of the Zone, then again to the South, - as my aunt used to say - to shit and not live! If they keep on screwing us like this, then we'll never find anything. And I have debts to pay on the mainland. They're fine, they go to sleep with a clear conscience, and I... 
Raven, when we were still at the Bar, took me and cracked me open. I'm sitting on a bench, smoking, and I can't get my head around it. I keep thinking: how are my people outside the perimeter, are they still alive? Before fleeing to the Zone, I sent them secretly to his mother in the village, but this scumbag Koreytsa has long arms ... So unhappy thoughts overtake me. And then this geezer comes up, does his easy walk, carefree, drops down next to me on a bench and says: "What, you need money? How much?" I was surprised at first: I don't recall having blabbed about my personal life here, except possibly while drunk. But then I figured: anyone can guess that stalkers come here mainly for the money, and if one of them has a sour face in the morning, as I did, then he has no money and is in dire need of it. I say to him, "Who doesn't need it?" - And I turn away. And he takes a pile of bills out of his pocket, slams them on the bench, and says, "Just take it, and when you come back from your expedition, we'll settle accounts with you." I said to him, "And the interest?" He just grinned in reply, got up, and left. That was it. 

 %c[255,255,128,0]I went to the factory, and there were soldiers there. Shit, I've got a cache there! Inside of the complex under a bush by the wall on the south side...%c[default]

 %c[255,255,128,0]I went to the factory, and there were soldiers there. Shit, I've got a cache there! Inside of the complex under a bush by the wall on the south side...%c[default]

entries.EN:
By the Captain's order, passed through the messenger, we arrived at the Agroprom together with Patsyuk. He whined the whole way that he was tired of these long hikes, I had to shout at him to shut him up. It worked, after the army warehouses he didn't speak once. By the way, I did not like such a change of plans either: everything was prepped, checked tenfold, only to receive new orders. Apparently, the Captain had some doubts. But we'll wait for the signal, there's nothing else to do. 
I remembered an incident recently. When we first started preparations, we held regular team meetings at our "base" near the Bar. I remember things were tight at the time, there weren't enough people, not enough weapons and ammo. Nobody wanted to risk their lives for who knows what. To top it off, the bandits somehow found out that we were saving our money for something big and started trying to intercept us. In general, a bad streak of misfortune. But one evening, the Captain, cheerful and singing to himself, comes to us in the hangar and says: that's it, the expedition will take place! It turns out that he was able to find people who liked our idea - it was stalkers from the Hunters' Association. They were part of a group that would catch the local mutants for the scientists. So these hunters decided to help us, taking into account that we will then help them in their operations, as they themselves are too few in numbers in the Zone. That evening, all of us unanimously voted in favor, and the fate of the expedition was sealed. 

 %c[255,255,128,0]There's a cliff by the swamp with a large tree on it. And on that tree is my backpack.%c[default]
